assessment.intent: Give local and service-area businesses a practical standard for location pages that provide genuine local value, avoid thin doorway-page patterns, and connect naturally to services, proof, and contact paths.
assessment.specificity: Strong and concrete: names the Okanagan communities Michael serves, describes real service-area boundary decisions (travel, minimums, seasonal access), and includes a usable six-block page structure with purposes.
assessment.evidence: Appropriate and restrained. Two Google sources support the doorway-page and local ranking framing, plus one Michael project (Cool Runnings) used as a brief illustration without invented metrics. No unsupported percentages, tests, or client anecdotes.
assessment.voice: Consistent with Michael's voice: connected conversational sentences, Canadian spelling, a clear opinion (a simple well-written page beats an expensive design around repeated text), constructive and mostly caveat-free. No flagged phrases, no em dashes, no corporate padding.
assessment.usefulAsset: Yes. The outline table, the 'what each city page needs' checklist, and the decision rule for when to build more pages make this a reusable resource for Okanagan and Okanagan-adjacent service businesses planning their 2027 site structure.
